reasons: Lake identity gives case_name United States v. Burgess, court 10th Cir., date_decided 2009-08-11, and year 2009.
Lake citations list official cite 576 F.3d 1078, parallel cite 80 Fed. R. Serv. 344, and vendor cites 2009 U.S. App. LEXIS 17823 and 2009 WL 2436674.
residual_risks: The cached opinion caption says No. 08-8053 while the content/lake docket field says 08-3072; docket was not part of this inventory assertion.

defect.evidence_quote: Following a traffic stop and a canine alert, police searched David Burgess’ motor home for drugs and evidence of drug trafficking.
defect.problem: The disclosed opinion/lake record does not support placing Burgess on a Border Searches home, even as cross-doctrine. The opinion is a traffic-stop, automobile-exception, warrant-particularity, and computer-search-scope case; no disclosed text supplies a border-search holding or application.
defect.proposed_fix: Remove the Border Searches home/tag unless a disclosed border-search authority or home-page rationale ties Burgess to border device searches.

reasons: The cached opinion frames the facts as a Wyoming traffic stop and canine alert, not a border encounter.
The only disclosed occurrences of border-related language are in the content page’s own tag/claim, not in the opinion or lake authority record.
residual_risks: A broader corpus page might use Burgess analogically for border device searches, but that support is not disclosed here.

reasons: The opinion states the warrant authorized search of the motor home for drug-trafficking evidence, including computer records and pay-owe/address-book/rolodex material.

The opinion holds the warrant was sufficiently particular when read with context and the incorporated affidavit, and that Hughes stopped after encountering suspected child pornography and obtained a new warrant.
The court affirmed denial of suppression and stated: On these facts, we cannot say the Fourth Amendment was violated.
residual_risks: Lake pinpoints[] is empty, so support rests on the cached opinion text rather than a lake pinpoint quote field.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: For precision, say Agent Hughes, rather than officers, initially encountered the suspected child-pornography image and then stopped to obtain a second warrant.

defect.evidence_quote: Here Hughes immediately stopped the preview upon seeing an instance of suspected child pornography and obtained another warrant to search for pornography.
defect.problem: The opinion supports a digital search-scope/inadvertent-discovery discussion, but the disclosed text does not expressly invoke the Plain View Doctrine or make Burgess a key plain-view holding. Calling the case Key for Plain View is broader than the disclosed evidence supports.
defect.proposed_fix: Downgrade to Related, or retitle the role as digital computer-search scope/inadvertent discovery; reserve Key for a home on computer-search particularity or warrant scope.

reasons: The opinion’s operative reasoning is warrant particularity, scope of search, Carey limits, and alternatively Leon good faith.
The cached text contains no express plain-view-doctrine formulation; the child-pornography discovery was treated through search scope and the later second warrant.
residual_risks: If the Plain View Doctrine home page defines itself to include Carey-style digital inadvertent-discovery cases, that home-page evidence was not disclosed.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use Related rather than Key unless the corpus supplies an internal rationale making Burgess a leading plain-view-digital case.
